references.text: The disciples went and found everything just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal. [ref:Luk 22:13|Luke 22:13] shows the fulfillment of the mission Jesus gave to Peter and John in verse 8.
The parallel account in [ref:Mark 14:13-16|Mark 14:13-16] tells how Jesus sent two of his disciples to prepare the Passover meal, with detailed instructions to follow a man carrying a water jar.
In [ref:Matt 26:17-19|Matthew 26:17-19], the parallel account is told where the disciples ask Jesus where he wants them to prepare the Passover meal, and he sends them to a specific man in the city.

The Passover lamb was to be prepared according to God's instruction in [ref:2 Mos 12:3-6|Exodus 12:3-6], which gives detailed instructions on selecting and preparing the Passover lamb—the original background for the meal Peter and John were sent to prepare.
In [ref:2 Mos 12:8-11|Exodus 12:8-11], instructions are given on how the Passover meal should be eaten, forming the basis of the tradition that Jesus and his disciples followed.

[ref:5 Mos 16:1-8|Deuteronomy 16:1-8] contains the regulations for celebrating Passover, including the command to eat unleavened bread and slaughter the Passover lamb—the law-based background for the preparations Jesus requested.

Peter and John are often mentioned together as an inner circle among the disciples. In [ref:Luk 8:51|Luke 8:51], Jesus takes Peter, John, and James inside to Jairus' daughter, showing the special trust Jesus had in these disciples.

Peter and John also act together after Jesus' resurrection, for example in [ref:Apg 3:1|Acts 3:1], where they go up to the temple together—a testimony to the close cooperation between these two disciples.
In [ref:Apg 8:14|Acts 8:14], Peter and John are sent to Samaria by the apostles, showing that they continued to work together as a pair after Pentecost, just as Jesus had sent them together here.
